conservation_status.value: near extinction around 1950, recovered from 1983; small population, 243 hens/153 cocks (2019)

history_summary.value: The Appenzeller Spitzhauben has been bred in the Swiss Alps for centuries, though its exact origins are unclear and it may relate to the Brabanter of the Low Countries. It nearly went extinct around 1950 but was revived from 1983 with help from ProSpecieRara, hatching 230 chicks that year.
